design: 30 integer-list concepts across reductions, projections, maps, filters, compositions, and out-of-inventory controls; 4 revealed and 3 held-out examples per task

tasks.request_text: Write a function that returns the sum of the list.
Write a function that returns the number of items in the list.
Write a function that returns the largest item in the list.
Write a function that returns the smallest item in the list.
Write a function that returns the first item in the list.
Write a function that returns the last item in the list.
Write a function that returns the list in reverse order.
Write a function that adds two to every item in the list.
Write a function that adds five to every item in the list.
Write a function that subtracts three from every item in the list.
Write a function that multiplies every item in the list by three.
Write a function that replaces every item with its absolute value.
Write a function that keeps only items greater than two.
Write a function that keeps only items greater than negative one.
Write a function that keeps only negative items.
Write a function that keeps only even items.
Write a function that keeps only items equal to zero.
Write a function that returns the sum of only the positive items.
Write a function that returns the sum of only the negative items.
Write a function that returns the sum of the squares of all items.
Write a function that returns the sum of only the even items.
Write a function that counts the positive items.
Write a function that returns the product of all items.
Write a function that keeps positive items and returns them in reverse order.
Write a function that returns the sum of the absolute values of the items.
Write a function that returns how many positive items are in the list.
Write a function that counts the even items in the list.
Write a function that returns the smallest positive item.
Write a function that returns the median item in the list.
Write a function that counts the distinct items in the list.
